description:
GOAL: run a real program. `Json.decode/1` + `Json.encode/1` written in fz, with a
hand-written Elixir twin as the oracle and pinned allocation goldens. Today the
largest program fz has ever run is ~22 executable lines (behavior/quicksort.fz);
JSON is ~300-400 lines across 4-6 modules.

SIGNAL:
  - `oracle_goldens_match_elixir` -- real Elixir owns expected.txt, so `fz == Elixir`
    holds transitively across run/interp/build.
  - `Process.heap_alloc_stats()` goldens on a real workload, not an 11-element list.
  - round-trip: decode(encode(x)) == x, independent of stdout.

STRATEGY: work backwards from the goal. JSON demands exactly the missing library --
scanning demands String + native bitstring dispatch; objects demand a real Map;
arrays demand the Enum builders; numbers demand Integer/Float format; output demands
IO. Each gap becomes a demand-driven ticket rather than a taste-driven port.

WHY NOW -- the compiler is ahead of the library. TRMC + owned-cons reuse already hit
the hand-written floor (quicksort pins list_cons_bytes=176, struct_bytes=0,
closure_bytes=0, no annotations). The library squanders it. Measured at N=20,
input literal = 20 cells:

  op                        HEAD   floor
  Enum.to_list               60      20
  Enum.map                   80      40
  Enum.filter                60      20
  Enum.map |> Enum.filter   120      40

Cause: `fn to_list(enumerable), do: reverse(reverse(enumerable))` (enum.fz:46), and
every builder routes through it.

RESEARCH CORRECTIONS (measured at 67e09d373, not assumed):
  - fz does NOT need `is_*` guard BIFs. Type-annotated clause heads (`x :: integer`)
    subsume them, statically AND dynamically -- verified dispatching on values that
    arrive through a mailbox as `any`. List.flatten/1 was written and runs natively
    matching Elixir. The only constraint: `::` binds at top-level param positions
    only, so nested type dispatch needs a one-line helper.
  - Native bitstring matching is NOT missing. native_codegen/receive.rs:654 -> :1083
    implements Region::Bitstring completely; jobs/native.rs:3092 errors on the same
    region. One emitter, two callers -- a fold, not a build.
  - Externs CAN return binaries (fz_binary_concat proves it). File/String primitives
    are reachable; the cost is that each allocating extern is hand-special-cased in
    ~4 places (31 rungs already in prim.rs).

DECIDED (2026-09-06):
  - `/` adopts Elixir semantics: always float; add div/2 and rem/2.
  - `def`/`defp` added as aliases for `fn`/`fnp`.
  - Inspect becomes a real protocol (requires fz-kdt.11 first).
  - Goal program is JSON round-trip.

OUT OF SCOPE, documented as divergence: charlists (.agent/docs/charlists.md),
regex/sigils, Stream.

BASELINE AT ARC START: cargo test --lib 1962/0/6ig; fixture_matrix 540/0
(--test-threads=1). Both verified green at 67e09d373.

comments.text: Draft PR for the arc: https://github.com/jallum/fz/pull/122 (branch fz-lib). Commits land there one ticket at a time as they are cold-reviewed.

CI on PR #122 has been silently dead, and the cause is now verified.

The arc branch is stacked on fz-tfn/denotational-identity. That base moved while this work was in flight -- it absorbed PR #110 (fz-kdt arc) and PR #118 (fz-tfn recalculator) -- so PR #122 went mergeable: CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus: DIRTY, and GitHub Actions creates NO check suites for a conflicting PR. No error, no skipped status, nothing:

  commits/5c2a0483e/check-suites -> total_count 0
  commits/6b9c521e9/check-suites -> total_count 1   (the one run; FAILED on fz2_cli census pins)
  commits/c29520325/check-suites -> total_count 0
  commits/ffd13dcb6/check-suites -> total_count 0

So the red X the PR displays is from 6b9c521e9, whose failure was fixed in
c29520325 -- a commit CI never ran. Three of four pushes have no independent
verification at all; 'verified green' currently rests entirely on the six local
targets.

REMEDY: merge the updated base branch into fz-lib (not main -- the base is the
stack's branch), which clears the conflict and lets Actions fire again. Re-check
mergeable after every base advance rather than trusting an earlier CLEAN.

Worth knowing for the rest of the epic: this base is ACTIVE and will keep
moving, so this will recur. If the stack lands into main, retargeting #122 to
main becomes the simpler arrangement.

title: fz stdlib: run a real program -- JSON round-trip on an Elixir-parity runtime library
